implementation_versions.vep_stim: 0.1.0a1 @ 5367ef4afb976271ecc6297b70a95dd3d944af61 (installed package NOT modified; patched copies in work/T0029)

patches.what: Package loops i in (10*ns+1):(nt*ns) over the column-major to_vector(xhat2[nt,ns]) and so drops the first floor(10*ns/nt) channels entirely (P2 gain: channels 0-11 plus 10 steps of channel 12) instead of the first 10 time points. Fixed to drop time rows 1..10 for every channel.
patches.verification: verify_patch.py: patched Stan lp equals a numpy re-implementation (diff 0.02 = CSV rounding); the package model equals numpy with the column-major mask up to the 26740*log(sqrt(2*pi)) normalising constant (diff -24572.4), confirming the defect.

patches.what: Scalar triple loop replaced by gx = SC*x - rowsum(SC).*x and matrix sensor projection; same Euler scheme and parameterisation. ~30 ms per L-BFGS iteration vs ~0.2 s/gradient reported in T0026.
GQ block removed; PPC recomputed in numpy from draws.
sfreq derived from time_steps (P2: 8 ms -> 125 Hz) instead of the notebooks' hard-coded 250 Hz, so hpf/lpf cut-offs are where intended. Used only for the noise calibration from P2 SEEG.

No N(0,0.2) noise padding around a window whose CROSS-CHANNEL mean (axis=0) was removed; instead the authors' P2 recipe of a real post-ictal baseline segment prepended and PER-CHANNEL baseline referencing, so channels with DC offset get no step artefact.
seeg_log_power zero-padded the end of the signal, so the last 100 samples' log-power decays artificially; reflect padding instead.
u_star ~ N(0,10) instead of N(0,1); L-BFGS only; used to diagnose the amplitude/offset bias; not part of pass/fail.

consumed_case.inputs: A0067-DatasetCard P2_SEEG_ts_fit.npz (SC, gain; P2 SEEG only for noise calibration) and P1_SEEG_SEEG_fit.npz (SC only, arm B)

fitting_partitions.note: Synthetic single-seizure case; no cohort split, no reserved outcomes. Whole simulated window (150 steps; first 10 excluded from the likelihood) used for fitting in both arms.
fitting_partitions.arm_B: SC = P1 template (same VEP atlas), gain = P2
fitting_partitions.identical_data: both arms fit the identical Obs matrix (sha256 a6fec8bfd6855fe6ca87554a30b9d7991b63703f6b35e479400eb472bc2bc88e)

observation_model.fit: log(Obs[t,s]) ~ Normal(amp*(gain@x)[s,t] + u[s], eps), t = 11..150 (patched: first 10 time points skipped for every channel)
observation_model.generating: log-feature = amp*(gain@x) + u + AR(1) noise (phi 0.9, marginal sd 0.15; realised sd 0.146) - iid assumption of the fit is deliberately violated

predictive_checks.note: Deterministic mean path at 100 thinned draws per arm; R2 within channel over all 191 channels ~0.25 because most channels carry only noise; informative channels (clean deflection > 2 noise sd) = 11, 12, 13, 14, 81, 82.

recovery_benchmark.planted: EZ Right-Amygdala x0=-1.6 (only seizing region, onset step 80); PZ Right-Hippocampus-anterior, Right-Rhinal-cortex x0=-2.1 (sub-threshold, do not seize); amp 0.1, K 1
recovery_benchmark.note: Both arms over-estimate the extent: the sub-threshold PZ and Right-Insula-gyri-longi are estimated EZ-like (x0 -1.6 to -1.73) and seize in 100% of posterior draws, while amp is estimated at ~0.05 (half the truth). Arm B looking better than arm A is most plausibly an initialisation effect (its best L-BFGS optima happened to be EZ-first modes), not evidence that a mismatched SC helps.

identifiability.amplitude_vs_extent: amp x number of co-seizing regions is a near-flat direction: the EZ is seen by 3 contacts (max gain 8.1) that also see R-Hippocampus-anterior, R-Rhinal-cortex and R-Insula-gyri-longi, so half the amplitude with 3-4 co-seizing neighbours reproduces the sensor data (PPC R2 0.87 on the 6 informative channels vs data, 0.92 vs the noise-free signal) with the wrong network.
identifiability.offset_prior_conflict: u~N(2,1) and amp's half-normal prior penalise the realistic intercepts (planted u_star up to 20.5), pulling amp down and favouring regions that seize for the whole window (they act as channel offsets). Sensitivity S1 (u_star sd 10, L-BFGS) raised amp to 0.06-0.077 and reduced co-seizing neighbours, but the optima still disagreed (EZ rank 1-5) with spurious early/whole-window seizing regions (e.g. R-T2-anterior, gain 47.6, seizing from step 9).
identifiability.x0_vs_z_init: x0 and z_init trade off for onset timing; low-gain regions can be fitted as seizing early (R-Insula-gyri-longi ~step 48 in some optima), absorbing AR(1)-correlated noise that the iid likelihood treats as signal.
identifiability.coupling: K weakly identified (posterior mean 0.39 in A, 0.79 in B; truth 1); with P2 SC weights to the EZ of 0.03-0.06 the coupling barely shapes the data, which is why swapping in P1 SC changed little.
identifiability.unobserved_regions: Spearman(posterior mean x0, true x0) only ~0.11-0.12 over 162 regions: most regions are invisible to the 191 contacts and stay at the prior.

intended_use: pipeline qualification benchmark only (synthetic virtual patient; not a clinical prediction, not evidence about Wang P1/P2 or any HUP patient; a fitted posterior is not a calibrated probability of seizure freedom)
implications_for_HUP: Even with the matching connectome, the correct gain, the model's own forward model and the channel-skip bug fixed, vep-stim did not meet the convergence criterion and over-estimated EZ extent (4-5 EZ-like regions for one planted EZ). Template-connectome fits of HUP patients should therefore not be used for x0 maps, EZ extent or a single 'the EZ' call; at most for rank-based, ensemble-reported hypothesis generation with the multimodality shown explicitly.

The template-SC arm was not worse than the matching-SC arm here (EZ 1st in all arm-B chains): with weak SC weights and K ~0.4-0.8 the inference is driven by gain and onset timing, so SC mismatch is a second-order error next to the identifiability problems. One seed and one EZ only: this does not show that a template SC is safe in general (e.g. for EZs whose spread runs through strong SC edges).

The package likelihood bug drops the first 10*ns likelihood terms in column-major order: here channels 0-11 entirely plus steps 1-110 of channel 12, i.e. two of the six informative EZ channels lose all or most of their onset. In this instance it did NOT change the MAP ranking (the 3 converged high-amp unpatched optima ranked the EZ 1st with 3 FPs, because channel 13 and late channel 12 still carry the EZ signal; 3 vs 5 optima is too few to compare with the patched ensemble). It is still a correctness defect whose damage depends on where informative contacts fall in the channel order; HUP fits must use the patched likelihood (P1).

The u/amp priors must be data-centred (or features baseline-referenced) before HUP fitting; otherwise realistic feature offsets push amplitude toward its bound and create whole-window seizing artefacts.

NUTS needs a reparameterisation or a different sampler setup: every draw hit max_depth 8 (step size ~0.007-0.015); 600 iterations took ~55 min per chain here. Budget several hours per patient, start multiple chains from diverse optima, and treat R-hat > 1.05 as a hard stop.
deviations_from_package_recipe: Synthetic data generated at the model's own observation level (log-feature = amp*gain@x + u + noise) rather than as raw SEEG passed through the feature pipeline, so arm A tests inference, not the feature pipeline; the fixed feature pipeline was used only to calibrate realistic noise/levels from P2's simulated SEEG.

Observation noise AR(1) (phi 0.9, sd 0.15) instead of the iid noise the likelihood assumes (deliberate, realistic: the 1 Hz low-pass in the pipeline makes feature noise strongly autocorrelated; P2 baseline lag-1 AC ~0.91).

Design iteration before any fit (simulation only, logged): first draft amp=0.015 gave max channel deflection 0.34 (2.3 noise SD, 1 channel) - judged unrealistically weak vs P2 feature ranges; amp raised to 0.10 and channel intercepts set to give P2-like baseline levels (~3.5). PZ x0 -2.1 kept although coupling-driven recruitment does not occur (P2 SC weights to the EZ 0.03-0.06; higher K suppresses rather than recruits in this model).

L-BFGS: 10 starts/arm with package settings (lbfgs tol_param=1e-10 iter=20000 init=5) plus 16 starts/arm with tightened tol_rel_grad=1e2, tol_rel_obj=1e1, tol_grad=1e-10 because package defaults stopped at ||grad|| up to 15 inside a prior-driven low-amp basin (package uses 50 starts on a cluster).
NUTS: 6 chains/arm = best 3 L-BFGS optima x 2 (package: best 8 x 2), warmup 300 / samples 300 (package 500/500), adapt delta 0.9 and max_depth 8 (package 0.99 / 7, which saturated in T0026).
CmdStan 2.40.0 instead of README-pinned 2.21.0; direct exe calls instead of GNU parallel.
